order_wins: **Texmaco Rail & Engineering (TEXRAIL)** — **two orders aggregating Rs 131.36 crore including taxes**: Rs 106.88 cr from Touax Texmaco Railcar Leasing for four BFNS22.9 rakes, and Rs 24.48 cr from Transport Corporation of India for one ACT-1 rake. Texmaco co-promotes Touax, making the larger leg a related-party order _(~2.8% of mcap)_.

**Airfloa Rail Technology (AIRFLOA)** — a **Letter of Acceptance of Rs 31.08 crore from the Rail Coach Factory, Kapurthala**, received 25 August, for interior furnishing of one 16-car Namo Bharat Rapid Rail rake, for completion by February 2027 _(~2.7% of mcap)_.

**Artson (ARTSON)** — a **purchase order of Rs 7,17,00,000 excluding taxes from L&T-MHI Power Boilers Private Limited**, for supply of 24 vessels for three boilers at NTPC Nabinagar (units 4, 5 and 6), delivered by February, May and August 2027 _(~1.1% of mcap)_.

**Refex Renewables & Infrastructure (REFEXRENEW)** — wholly owned **Refex Green Power wins an SJVN letter of award to build an 80 MW wind project**, with a 25-year power purchase agreement to follow. The filing states no tariff or project value.

**GRE Renew Enertech (GRERENEW)** — reports **eight solar EPC orders aggregating Rs 24,88,37,335 received between 16 and 31 August**, seven ground-mounted captive plants and one rooftop; its fortnightly update masks every customer name _(~9.4% of mcap)_.

**Anupam Rasayan India (ANURAS)** — signs a **six-year specialty-chemical supply contract with a US-headquartered speciality metal manufacturer**, dispatches starting in the second half of Q3 FY27. The annexure ties consideration to quantities delivered, so no value is disclosed.
fund_raises_fresh_equity: **SRM Contractors (SRM)** — **up to 19,34,236 warrants at Rs 517, aggregating Rs 100,00,00,012 for cash**, to promoters Sanjay Mehta and Puneet Pal Singh in equal halves, plus a **QIP not exceeding Rs 150 crore**; both go to the 30 September AGM _(~14.1% of mcap)_.

**Vishnu Prakash R Punglia (VPRPL)** — board approves **raising up to Rs 100,00,00,000 by warrants convertible into equity on a preferential basis** to Promoter Group and Non-Promoter Public allottees; the number, issue price, allottees and conversion terms are all left to the directors _(~22.1% of mcap)_.

**Sarveshwar Foods (SARVESHWAR)** — **up to 22,25,00,000 fully convertible warrants of Re 1 face value at Rs 3.80 each, aggregating to Rs 84,55,00,000 for cash**, to Promoter & Promoter Group and Non-Promoter Public allottees named in an annexure, subject to shareholders' approval _(~20.4% of mcap)_.

**Som Distilleries & Breweries (SDBL)** — **up to 32,12,955 convertible warrants of Rs 2 face value at Rs 77.81, aggregating Rs 25,00,00,028.55**, to promoter Deepak Arora for working capital, subject to approval at the 29 September AGM _(~1.7% of mcap)_.

**Ken Enterprises (KEN)** — **up to 39,97,000 convertible warrants at Rs 40.50 each (Rs 30.50 premium), aggregating Rs 16,18,78,500 for cash**, to named promoters; the same board proposed varying the objects of its IPO proceeds _(~16.9% of mcap)_.

**TMT India (TMTIND)** — approves a **preferential issue of up to 7,21,65,000 shares at Rs 10 for cash**, plus a 2,05,00,000-share swap issue to buy **100% of Shakti Auto Industries**, and a tenfold authorised-capital increase to Rs 100 crore. All needs shareholder approval.

**P.M. Telelinnks (PMTELE)** — approves a **preferential issue of up to 1,50,00,000 shares at Rs 10, aggregating up to Rs 15,00,00,000 for cash** to non-promoter allottees, with authorised capital going from Rs 12 crore to Rs 27 crore; subject to shareholders' approval _(~100% of mcap)_.
equity_allotments: **Asston Pharmaceuticals (ASSTON)** — allots **24,10,431 shares at Rs 115 each (Rs 105 premium) to 15 investors** on a preferential basis, Vijay Rathee taking 13,17,391 of them. That is Rs 27.72 crore on our arithmetic; the filing states no aggregate.

**Fonebox Retail (FONEBOX)** — receives **NSE in-principle approval to issue 30,00,000 shares at Rs 85.80** to promoters Pankaj Vasudeva and Dhrumil Shah and to public allottee Rajesh Shah, 10,00,000 each — Rs 25.74 crore on our arithmetic, the filing stating no aggregate _(~25.1% of mcap)_.
**Shyam Metalics and Energy (SHYAMMETL)** — grants **11,000 stock options to a single eligible employee** under its ESIP-2023 performance scheme, each option carrying one Rs 10 share.
m_and_a: **Tata Motors (TMCV)** — TML CV Holdings B.V. **commences the recommended all-cash voluntary tender offer for all Iveco Group common shares at EUR 14.1 cum dividend**, on a Consob-approved offer document; the acceptance period runs 7 September to 26 October, and Exor, Iveco's largest shareholder, has irrevocably committed to tender ~27.06%.

**IndiGrid Infrastructure Trust (INDIGRID)** — executes **securities purchase agreements dated 4 September to acquire Shongtong Power Transmission at an enterprise value not exceeding INR 53,158 million**, payable only once the project is complete and earning, and subject to unitholder approval. Seller Enerica ReGrid Infra is a related party.

**Shivansh Finserve (SHIVA)** — acquires **11,18,149 shares, or 19.50% of Startech Infralogistics, for Rs 42,48,96,620 at Rs 380 per share**, discharged entirely in paper by issuing up to 2,12,44,831 of its own shares at Rs 20 each; Startech becomes an investee company.

**EFC (I) (EFCIL)** — **completes the sale of 100% of wholly owned subsidiary Sanvritti Alpha for INR 39,00,00,000**, monetising two floors of Pune's Konark Alpha building to an unrelated buyer. It is an "Assets Sale and Lease Back", so EFC keeps operating the space _(~1.4% of mcap)_.

**Classic Filaments (CFL)** — board notes the **completed acquisition of 51% of Procasts Engineering**, an aluminium die-casting business with provisional FY26 turnover of Rs 31.20 crore, which becomes a subsidiary; the two companies' promoters are common and the consideration is not stated.

**Transworld Shipping Lines (TRANSWORLD)** — signs a memorandum of agreement to buy the **vessel Valsamitis from Greenland Marine of Monrovia, Liberia, for US$ 11,750,000**, an unrelated party. No rupee equivalent appears in the filing, so none is given and no ratio is struck.

**Sudarshan Pharma Industries (SUDARSHAN)** — board approves buying **24,23,675.64 shares, or 9.50%, of Delaware-incorporated MedTherapy Biotechnology** for cash in US dollars; its chairman and joint MD take a further 3,82,685.63 shares personally. The price is left to a valuation and is not stated.

**RDB Real Estate Constructions (RDB)** — buys **an additional 10% of associate RDB Anekant Orbit Properties, taking its holding to 51%** and turning the investee into a subsidiary on completion. The consideration is not stated in the filing.

**FSN E-Commerce Ventures (NYKAA)** — **completes the further 24.2% increase in its shareholding in subsidiary Earth Rhythm**, approved by the board on 21 May, with the shares credited to its demat account. No consideration is stated.

**The Phoenix Mills (PHOENIXLTD)** — NCLT Chennai **sanctions the merger of six step-down subsidiaries into Astrea Real Estate Developers**, itself a subsidiary; a purely internal reorganisation first intimated in January 2025, with no consideration leaving the group.

**Lactose (India) (LACTOSE)** — its **amalgamation with Vitanosh Ingredients became effective on 5 September**, the certified NCLT Ahmedabad order of 20 August having been filed with the Registrar of Companies that day.

**ASK Automotive (ASKAUTOLTD)** — its joint venture **ASK GTD Control Cables began commercial production and supply at Karoli, Rajasthan**, a year after the JV was incorporated. No capacity or investment figure is given.

**EPIC Energy (EPIC)** — its joint venture **Swachcha Urja Nirman LLP began trial production at a second-life battery assembly plant at Wada, Maharashtra**, repurposing retired lithium-ion cells; commercial production is planned for early October.

**Sellwin Traders (SELLWIN)** — **abandons its August 2025 MOU with Global Market Insights IT Service LLC**: due diligence found the proposed holding-subsidiary arrangement not commercially viable, no definitive agreement was signed and the MOU has expired.
capex_core: **Shakti Pumps (India) (SHAKTIPUMP)** — **invests Rs 11.00 crore in cash for equity of wholly owned Shakti Energy Solutions**, which is building a greenfield **2.20 GW solar DCR cell and PV module plant at Pithampur, Madhya Pradesh**; intra-group funding.

**Tata Consultancy Services (TCS)** — subsidiary **HyperVault has secured 264 acres in Hyderabad for an AI data centre campus of up to 1 GW**, purpose-built for frontier AI companies and hyperscalers with liquid-cooled high-density GPU compute, to be built out in phases against customer demand.

**NLC India (NLCINDIA)** — board approves an **unsecured external commercial borrowing of USD 100 million from Punjab National Bank** for the capex of its thermal, mining and diversification projects. It is debt, so it ranks nowhere, and the same meeting fixed a 22 September dividend record date.
business_updates: **Results season** — 4 companies filed results / earnings-call material today (press releases, recordings, transcripts, presentations) — tracked in the Results tab, not itemised here.

**JSW Steel (JSWSTEEL)** — **consolidated crude steel production of 24.65 lakh tonnes in August, up 3% year on year**, Indian operations 23.87 lakh tonnes at 88% capacity utilisation and Ohio 0.78 lakh tonnes, down 11%.

**Rhetan TMT (RHETAN)** — says it is **exploring entry into corrosion-resistant steel TMT bars** for coastal and marine construction, having just obtained BIS licences for Fe500D, Fe550 and Fe550D grades. It is an intention, not a commitment, and no investment or capacity figure is given.
distress_risk: **Mohini Health & Hygiene (MHHL)** — India Ratings **downgrades its long-term bank loans three notches to IND BB- from IND BBB-, outlook Negative, and its short-term loans to IND A4+ from IND A3**, on Rs 760.51 million of facilities. The covering letter calls it an affirmation; the agency says downgraded.

**International Combustion (India) (INTLCOMBQ)** — CRISIL **downgrades the long-term rating to CRISIL BBB-/Stable from BBB/Negative and the short-term rating to CRISIL A3 from A3+**, on Rs 125 crore of total bank loan facilities, with the outlook revised from Negative to Stable.
**H.G. Infra Engineering (HGINFRA)** — CARE **reaffirms CARE AA on Rs 140 crore of long-term bank facilities but revises the outlook from Stable to Negative**.

**Dhampur Bio Organics (DBOL)** — CARE **reaffirms CARE BBB+ and revises the outlook from Stable to Positive**, cutting rated long-term facilities to Rs 987.05 crore, on debt prepaid out of the June 2026 Meerganj sugar-unit slump sale.

**Ansal Properties & Infrastructure (ANSALAPI)** — files the certified **NCLT order of 24 July approving the resolution plan for its Fernhill project at Gurgaon**, the only part of the company the NCLAT confined the Section 7 insolvency to in January 2023.
**JCT (JCTLTD)** — its resolution professional convenes the **sixteenth meeting of the committee of creditors for 7 September** by video conference; the company remains under CIRP.

**Reliance Industries (RELIANCE)** — **step-down subsidiary Roptonal stands dissolved with effect from 18 August**, per a certificate issued by the Cyprus Department of Insolvency on 4 September. A housekeeping wind-up, with no figure attached.

**Harish Textile Engineers (HARISH)** — the **NCLT Mumbai has dismissed Kamlesh Corporation's insolvency petition as withdrawn**, the debt having been settled on consent terms of 19 August payable in instalments, with liberty to revive it on default.

**Galaxy Supermarket (GALAXY)** — the **NCLT has dismissed and disposed of the proceedings brought against it by the resolution professional of NuFuture Digital (India)**, first disclosed in November 2025; the company notes an appeal is possible.
other_notable: **BCPL Railway Infrastructure (BCPL)** — declared **lowest bidder (L-1) by Eastern Railway's Asansol division for replacement of overage structures in the Waria–Raniganj section, at a project cost of Rs 37.36 crore including GST** _(~32.6% of mcap)_. The annexure states the contract is yet to be received.

**Kellton Tech Solutions (KELLTONTEC)** — board **recommends raising up to USD 50 million through foreign currency convertible bonds** on private placement, in one or more tranches and subject to approvals. Convertible debt with no instrument terms fixed, so it ranks nowhere; no rupee equivalent is stated.

**Borana Weaves (BORANA)** — signs a **loan agreement to lend up to Rs 5,00,00,000 unsecured at 12% a year to Win Star Industries**, repayable on demand, an unrelated party in which it holds nothing. Money going out, not a joint venture _(~0.6% of mcap)_.
